title: Story Imprinting: AI Assistants Absorb Traits from Human Characters They Resemble
org: Truthful AI (with Harvard University, University of Oxford, METR)
why: Shows how an assistant persona absorbs traits from fiction it is trained on, a direct look at persona emergence. (our take)

title: ContextEcho: A Benchmark for Persona Drift in Long Agentic-Coding Sessions
why: Quantifies persona drift at scale across different model organizations and shows reset mechanisms fail, a critical empirical finding for understanding stability. (our take)

title: Attention Is All You Need
why: Introduced the transformer, the architecture every model we study runs on.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
why: Found: loss falls as a predictable power law in size, data and compute. Our take: the bet behind the scale-up.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
why: Found: in-context learning from examples in the prompt. Our take: where prompting as a craft starts.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT)
why: The RLHF recipe behind ChatGPT-style assistants. Our inference: the training loop later sycophancy research points to.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
why: Training against written principles instead of only human ratings. Our take: an early form of the 'spec' idea.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
why: 'Show your work' prompting. Our take: led to reasoning models and the faithfulness question.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
why: The think, act, observe loop behind most agent scaffolding, Lisa OS included.

title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
why: Found: the largest models were generally the least truthful. Our take: early evidence that capability isn't honesty.

title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
why: Found: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the true reason for a prediction.

title: Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations
why: Found: sycophancy worsens with model size; separately, more RLHF made some behaviors worse.

title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
why: The starting map for mechanistic interpretability: reading what attention layers compute.

title: Toy Models of Superposition
why: Models pack more features than neurons, so one neuron isn't one concept. Why later work turned to sparse autoencoders.

title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
why: Found: names side effects and reward hacking as core problems. The METR and Baker work picks this up.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
why: Found: 25 agents with memory and reflection showed unscripted social behavior. Our take: cousin to Raf's persona-emergence work.

title: Emergent Abilities of LLMs (Wei 2022) + Are Emergent Abilities of LLMs a Mirage? (Schaeffer 2023)
authors: Wei et al. / Schaeffer et al.
why: The claim and its rebuttal: apparent emergence may come from the choice of metric. Wei: arxiv.org/abs/2206.07682

title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Reasoning Models Varies with Where and How Preference Cues Are Delivered
why: Our take: this hits agents directly, because agents take in most of their information through tool returns. If CoT goes quiet exactly there, monitoring by reading the reasoning has a blind spot.

title: Suppressing Pressure, Amplifying Evidence: Self-Guided Attention Steering to Mitigate Sycophancy and Stubbornness
org: Purdue University / The Ohio State University / Analogy AI Inc. / The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen / Northwestern University
why: Direct evidence that models can be steered to resist sycophancy without trade-off to accuracy, using only the model's own reasoning. Raf would care because it shows a concrete mechanism for catching sycophancy during inference.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models ("Chinchilla")
why: Refines the Kaplan scaling laws already on your Fundamentals shelf: model size and training tokens should grow together. This is why later models trained on far more data.

title: Prompting Against Persona Drift: Comparing Intervention Timing and Content in LLM-Simulated Conversations
org: Zuse Institute Berlin / TU Berlin / Weizenbaum Institute
why: Our take: practical evidence on how to keep a system prompt in force over long conversations. The finding that what you re-inject matters more than when you do it applies directly to persona and scaffolding work.

title: AnthroDial: Benchmarking LLM Anthropomorphism in Autonomous Social Interaction
why: Addresses persona emergence in social interactions by studying how autonomous communication adapts across contexts and relationships. (our take)

title: MASC: A Multi-Agent Self-Calibration Framework with Latent Construct Alignment for Consistent Client Role-Playing in Psychological Counseling
why: Directly targets persona consistency in long dialogue, a core P1 concern. Shows multi-agent refinement reduces drift better than static prompts. (our take)

title: The System Prompt Illusion: How Instruction Preambles Modify Computation in Language Models
org: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
why: This reveals the mechanistic limits of system-prompt scaffolding: models parse safety instructions but don't act on them, while persona prompts reshape computation throughout. Raf would care because it explains why prompt-based safety is fragile and supports the need for training-level controls.

title: Lie to Me: How Faithful Is Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Reasoning Models?
org: University of Nevada, Las Vegas / DeepNeuro AI
why: Our take: this extends Turpin (on the Fundamentals shelf) to current open reasoning models. The reported gap (hints show up in the thinking tokens but drop out of the final answer) is a concrete faithfulness pattern you could test yourself.

title: Toward Robust Personalized Alignment for LLMs: Mitigating Persona Drift in Multi-Turn Dialogue
org: Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen) / Peng Cheng Laboratory / Huazhong University of Science and Technology
why: Directly addresses persona drift in long-turn dialogue, a core P1 concern. Shows that explicit turn-level vs. persistent-state separation improves robustness beyond memory or generation alone.

title: The Persona Hierarchy Model: Understanding Contextual Generalization in Fine-Tuning LLMs
why: Reveals personas act as a bottleneck for generalization, suggesting system-prompt contexts control behavior through a single underlying representation. (our take)
